source.citation: Shi, Z., Lothenbach, B. (2019). The role of calcium on the formation of alkali-silica reaction products. Cement and Concrete Research 126, 105898.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF): every table from the text layer, checked cell by cell against the page rendered at 150 dpi; the italic log Ks0 values of Table 6 identified from the font of the text layer (the italic face) and on the rendered page
transcription.note: Concentrations in mM as printed (mmol/L). The pH at 80 C is the authors' own correction, the value measured at 23 C minus 1.47 (Table 4 and 6, footnote); it is not a measurement at 80 C. A detection limit printed as '< 0.01' is transcribed as 0.01 with the column name listed in 'upper_limits'. The GEMS results of the paper (Figs. 7 and 10) are given only as figures and are not transcribed. The thermodynamic data of the three ASR products are solubility products at 80 C only: the paper gives no dfG, dfH, S, Cp or V for them.

temperature.description: Synthesis, equilibration and solubility-product temperature, 80 C.

equilibration_time.description: Equilibration time of the syntheses (precipitation experiments).

ph_measurement_temperature.description: Temperature at which the pH was measured, about 23 C.

ph_temperature_correction.location: Table 4 and Table 6, footnote b / a
ph_temperature_correction.description: pH units subtracted from the pH measured at 23 C to give the tabulated pH at 80 C.

dissolution_solid_mass.description: Dried synthesized solid re-dispersed in the dissolution (under-saturation) experiments.

dissolution_water_mass.description: Water of the dissolution experiments, at 80 C.

dissolution_time_months.description: Equilibration time of the dissolution experiments, in months as printed ('1 month'); not converted to days because the paper gives no day count.

koh_assay_minimum.description: Mass fraction: KOH pellets, '>= 85% KOH basis' (a lower bound, not the actual content); Shi and Lothenbach 2020 give 92 +/- 3 % from IC for the KOH they used.

naoh_assay_minimum.description: Mass fraction: NaOH pellets, '>= 99.9% NaOH basis'.

cao_burning_temperature.description: CaO obtained by burning calcium carbonate 12 h at 1000 C.

edh_ion_size_KOH.description: In angstrom (the unit of Lothenbach2019.json): common ion-size parameter of the extended Debye-Hueckel equation for KOH solutions.

edh_ion_size_NaOH.description: In angstrom (the unit of Lothenbach2019.json): common ion-size parameter of the extended Debye-Hueckel equation for NaOH solutions.

edh_b_gamma_KOH_25C.description: Semi-empirical third parameter b_y for KOH electrolyte at 25 C ('~0.123').

edh_b_gamma_NaOH_25C.description: Semi-empirical third parameter b_y for NaOH electrolyte at 25 C ('~0.098').

ca_impurity_SNC0.description: Ca measured in SNC0, to which no CaO was added (impurities of the starting materials); Table 6 prints it rounded, 0.04.

asr_product_solubility.location: Table 5, p. 5 (also Section 2.2.2, p. 4, for the formulas and the Ks0 expressions); the reaction column writes the printed Ks0 expression as a dissolution, with the Cemdata18 symbols of the species ({SiO2^0} = SiO2@)

KCaSi4O8(OH)3(H2O)2 = K+ + Ca+2 + 4 SiO2@ + 3 OH- + 2 H2O@

cnksh_end_members.location: Table 2, p. 3: standard properties at 25 C and 1 atm of the C-(N-)K-S-H solid solution; log Ks0 with respect to SiO(OH)3-, OH-, H2O, Ca2+, K+, Na+ (footnote a). INFCK is the paper's own end-member ('This study'); the others are cited from Myers et al. 2014 (ref. [34])

asr_product_compositions.location: Table 3, p. 4: molar ratios; 'gems_' = values selected for GEMS, 'edx_' = SEM/EDX, 'mb_' = mass balance, 'tga_' = TGA (from the authors' ref. [8]); null where the table prints a dash. The K-shlykovite GEMS selection is that of natural shlykovite (Pekov et al. 2010, footnote b), applied also to Na-shlykovite

solubility_experiments.location: Table 4, p. 4: precipitation (over-saturation, direct synthesis, 3 months, from the authors' ref. [8]) and dissolution (under-saturation, re-dispersed solids, 1 month) experiments at 80 C; null where the table prints a dash or nothing; pH_80C = pH_23C - 1.47; the log Ks0 are calculated (GEMS activities from the measured concentrations)

mixes.location: Table 1, p. 3: starting materials; the K series was made twice, with the high water content and with the low one printed in parentheses, here split into two rows ('K-high', 'K-low'); SKC0 has no low-water sample; the KOH and NaOH masses are the pellets as weighed (purity: quantities koh_assay_minimum, naoh_assay_minimum); Ca_Si, alkali_Si and Ca_alkali are the nominal molar ratios

solutions.location: Table 6, p. 6: solutions after 90 days at 80 C, phases from XRD, bulk solid composition from mass balance (solid_alkali_Si is K/Si for the K series, Na/Si for the Na series: the table prints the Na-series values in its K/Si column), and log Ks0 at 80 C; null where the table prints a dash or nothing; 'upper_limits' names the columns printed as '< value'; pH_80C = pH_23C - 1.47. The log Ks0 printed in italics (footnote c: very high Si, for comparison only, not used in the selected values) are listed in 'italic_log_Ks0'. SKC0.1 with high water: bottle broken, no data (Fig. 4 caption)

notes: The solubility products are equilibrium constants at 80 C (353.15 K) of the dissolution reactions written in asr_product_solubility, the species as printed: K+, Na+, Ca2+, SiO2^0 (Cemdata18 SiO2@), OH-, H2O. No standard property at 25 C is published for K-shlykovite, Na-shlykovite or ASR-P1, so a ThermoFun record needs an assumption for the temperature dependence; at 80 C itself any record that reproduces log Ks0(353.15 K) is equivalent.

The selected ASR-P1 value -27.1 is the mean of the five values the text names (Section 3.2 and Table 5): the two dissolution experiments of Table 4 (-26.5, -25.2) and the three precipitation experiments of Table 6 with Si < 100 mM (SKC0.4 high water -27.3, SKC0.5 high water -28.0, SKC0.5 low water -28.3); their mean is -27.06.

The C-S-H model is CNASH_ss of Myers et al. (2014) plus the K end-member INFCK, 'with a stability 0.5 log units lower than the Na-endmember' (Section 2.2.2). How INFCK enters the sublattice mixing of CNASH_ss is not stated.
The INFCN row of Table 2 agrees with the Cemdata18 ThermoFun record of INFCN to the printed digits except dfH: -2642.5 kJ/mol here, -2641.96 kJ/mol in the Cemdata18 file.

Table 2 refers the C-(N-)K-S-H solubility products to SiO(OH)3-; the companion paper (Shi and Lothenbach 2020, Table 2 footnote b) refers the same numbers to SiO2^0, and Shi et al. 2021 (Table A1 footnote a) to SiO2^0 and Al(OH)4-. The 2019 footnote is the one consistent with the Cemdata18 convention for CNASH_ss.

Samples SKC0.3 (high and low water) and SNC0.3 are the same mixes as SCK0.5 and SCN0.5 of Shi and Lothenbach 2020 (Ca/Si 0.3, alkali/Si 0.5, 60 or 30 g water) and repeat the same solution analyses, with small differences: Ca of SKC0.3 high water is 0.96 mM here and 0.33 mM there, and its ASR-P1 log Ks0 -26.0 (italic) here, -26.5 there; SKC0.3 low water -27.5 here, -27.3 there; SNC0.3 bulk Ca/Si 0.50 +/- 0.03 here, 0.49 +/- 0.04 there.
